name: Language school, tutoring or courses
description: A language school, tutoring service or course provider: course dates, the teachers, a price list and students' questions, with facts about what is taught, levels, class size, online or in-person teaching, accreditation, the placement test and refunds.

questions.question: Which languages or subjects do you teach?
questions.help: For example "English, German and Spanish" or "maths and physics for secondary school".

questions.question: Which levels do you teach?
questions.help: For example "A1 to C1 of the Common European Framework" or "from beginners to exam preparation".

questions.question: How many students are in a group?
questions.help: For example "4 to 8, individual lessons on request".

questions.question: Do you teach online, in person, or both?
questions.help: Say where the in-person lessons take place and which tool you use online.

questions.question: Is your school or are your courses accredited or certified? By whom?
questions.help: Only what you can prove with a document, with the issuing body and the number if there is one – e.g. an official exam centre. Leave it empty if there is none.

questions.question: How do new students find out which level they belong in?
questions.help: For example "free online placement test and a short interview with a teacher".

questions.question: What happens with the fee when a student cancels or misses lessons?
questions.help: In your own words, the same as in your terms, e.g. "full refund up to 7 days before the start, missed lessons can be made up in another group".

questions.question: Since which year have you been teaching?

audit.message: Add the next course dates – students look for when the next course starts.
Say which levels you teach – students need to know whether there is a course for them.
Introduce your teachers – students and parents want to know who will teach.
The price list has not changed for a year – check the course fees.
Add a contact e-mail in Business details – students and parents write with questions about courses.

claude: Students and parents want to know what is taught, at which level, when the next course starts, how big the groups are, what it costs and who teaches – put the subjects, the next course dates and the prices on the home page. Each course date is one item of the courses collection; a course held again is a new item, and a course that has started drops out of the list by itself. Never invent accreditations, exam-centre status, certificates, pass rates, success stories, teachers' qualifications or native speakers – state an accreditation only with the issuing body as the owner gives it. Do not promise a level or an exam result within a time. Refunds are a fact as the owner states them; consumer rules differ by country, so say they should be checked. Photos of children only with their parents' consent.
